title: A sufficiently fine fixed-mesh Riemann sum lies within an explicit, accuracy-derived distance of the integral
statement: For F, a <= b, and a uniform-continuity witness u, there is a threshold e0 such that for ANY mesh depth built as deep(e)+depth with e at least e0, and any further indices, the fixed-mesh Riemann sum riemannSum F a b m sits within an explicit, e-derived rational bound of CReal.integral F a b hab u. This is the Riemann-sum-vs-true-value estimate that was missing from the earlier riemannSum-only development: it compares ONE riemannSum at a FIXED mesh count against ITS OWN interval's integral, chaining riemannSum_shared_accuracy_close (fixed mesh vs a witness sample) with speedup_close (that sample vs the integral's own construction).

notes: theorem_dependency_inventory's direct-edge set for CReal.riemannSum_integral_close also includes CReal.riemannSum_sharedAccuracyClose, which is not a registered ledger fact; it is omitted from depends_on rather than registered speculatively. This estimate compares ONE riemannSum at a fixed mesh to ITS OWN interval's integral; it is the prerequisite for, but is NOT, CReal.integral_split (interval additivity), which remains open -- crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/creal/integral.rs's module documentation records an exact counterexample (m=0, f:=id, a:=0, c:=1, b:=3: riemannSum id 0 3 0 = 0 while the two halves sum to 2) showing the FIXED-MESH version of additivity is false, and states that only the limit (CReal.integral) version is even a candidate, still unproved. Do not register CReal.integral_split as proved or refuted from this fact.
